name: sqlite_freespace
description: Text fragments from the free space of a SQLite database's MAIN file: freelist pages, the unallocated gap of each b-tree page and the freeblock chain of freed cells. A fragment is text, not a row: no column, no table, no time, no row boundary, and the page may have belonged to something else. SENSITIVE: free pages of a messenger database hold message text and sometimes credentials, so the answer carries where each fragment is (finding_id, page, kind of region, byte offset, length in bytes and characters, encoding) and never its text; the text is written only on write_values: true, in a job run with secret_output: true, to $OUT/sqlite-freespace-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created before the scan, refused if it exists; the request is refused outside a job). Every offset is the byte position in the file and was read back from the file and compared before it was reported (offset_verified). Encodings: UTF-8 (any language) and UTF-16LE (Latin including Latin Additional, Greek including Greek Extended, Cyrillic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, Arabic, Devanagari, Thai and common punctuation; CJK, kana, Hangul and emoji only in runs of at least 8 characters, a lower-confidence reading; other scripts are not found), read at either byte parity, and UTF-16BE instead of UTF-16LE where the header declares UTF-16BE; text in another encoding, in a binary column or compressed or encrypted is not found, so a negative covers only those encodings and only the regions counted under scanned. A -wal, -shm or -journal beside the file is listed with its size and NOT examined: committed changes that only the WAL holds are absent, and a rollback journal's page images are not read; a -wal or -journal that holds bytes makes the status partial. The header is validated (page size, usable size, format versions, declared size against the file); the freelist is walked with a cycle check and compared with the header's count; every freeblock chain is checked for order, bounds and loops; lock-byte and pointer-map pages are skipped and counted. status is complete, partial (a time limit, a companion not read, pages not examined) or corrupt (the structure disagreed with itself where problems says; fragments found are still reported). A file that is not SQLite is refused with its size and, if it has 256 bytes or more, the entropy of its first 4 KiB, never its first bytes. contains narrows the sealed values file and nothing else: it needs write_values: true in a job run with secret_output: true (otherwise it is refused before anything is scanned), and the answer lists every fragment whatever the expression matched and does not say how many matched, since a list of the matches would tell, fragment by fragment, whether text you cannot see matches it. Whole results are kept: the inline page is limit rows and the rest is in the file the answer names. Not a deleted-record reconstruction, not a WAL or journal reader, and not a statement that a database was or was not vacuumed.

db.description: A SQLite database file (the main file; its -wal and -journal are listed, not read)

min_length.description: Shortest run of text, in characters (default 6, at least 3)

contains.description: Case-insensitive regex over a fragment's text; it decides which fragments' text is written to the values file (the answer lists all of them, and does not say which matched). Needs write_values: true, in a job run with secret_output: true. At most 1000 characters; a fragment on which it runs longer than 2 seconds (or past max_seconds) is counted under scanned.contains_timeouts and not written

limit.description: Fragments in the inline answer (default 200, and at most 1 MiB of rows); the whole list is in the file the answer names

write_values.description: Write each reported fragment's text to $OUT/sqlite-freespace-values.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; the answer never carries a text

max_seconds.description: Stop before the next page after this long (default 240, at most 270); the pages not reached are counted and the answer says partial
